query_snapshot: For hydrogen chloride, which barriers does the archived NIOSH table place in its 8-hour and 4-hour groups, and what additional hazard language appears in the entry?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- The archived NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing database organizes recommended protective clothing by columns labelled for 8-hour and 4-hour barrier groupings. [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective ...: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- The hydrogen chloride entry (NIOSH/CAMEO excerpt) includes the instruction: "PREVENT SKIN CONTACT (SOLUTION)". [HYDROGEN CHLORIDE, ANHYDROUS | CAMEO Chemicals | NOAA: https://cameochemicals.noaa.gov/chemical/8731; CDC - NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards -
Hydrogen chloride: https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/npg/npgd0332.html]
- The hydrogen chloride entry includes a FROSTBITE warning for compressed gases: compressed gases may create low temperatures on rapid expansion and appropriate protective clothing should be worn. [HYDROGEN CHLORIDE, ANHYDROUS | CAMEO Chemicals | NOAA: https://cameochemicals.noaa.gov/chemical/8731; CDC - NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards -
Hydrogen chloride: https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/npg/npgd0332.html]
- The hydrogen chloride entry advises that when wet or significantly contaminated (solution), work clothing should be removed and replaced. [HYDROGEN CHLORIDE, ANHYDROUS | CAMEO Chemicals | NOAA: https://cameochemicals.noaa.gov/chemical/8731]
